subject: Chemistry
central_question: How do partially filled d and f subshells explain the characteristic trends, variable oxidation states and chemistry of transition and inner-transition elements?
in_scope_units: Position and electronic configurations of d-block transition elements.
General physical properties, atomic and ionic sizes, ionisation enthalpies and enthalpies of atomisation.
Variable oxidation states and their stability in relation to electrode potentials.
Coloured ions, magnetic behaviour, complex formation, catalysis, interstitial compounds and alloys.
Preparation, properties and oxidising action of potassium dichromate and potassium permanganate.
Electronic configurations, oxidation states and chemical behaviour of lanthanoids and actinoids.
Lanthanoid contraction and comparison of lanthanoids with actinoids.
banned_topics: Detailed coordination-compound nomenclature and crystal-field splitting, which belong to Coordination Compounds.
Full extraction metallurgy of transition metals except the preparation routes specifically included for K₂Cr₂O₇ and KMnO₄.
Nuclear reactions of actinoids, which are outside this chemistry chapter.

known_pitfalls.claim: Every d-block element is a transition element.
known_pitfalls.correction: A transition element must have an incomplete d subshell in its atom or in at least one common ion; Zn, Cd and Hg have d¹⁰ configurations in their common states and are not transition elements.

known_pitfalls.claim: The 4s electrons are always removed after 3d electrons.
known_pitfalls.correction: On ionisation of first-row transition metals, 4s electrons are generally removed before 3d electrons.

known_pitfalls.claim: All transition-metal ions are coloured and paramagnetic.
known_pitfalls.correction: d⁰ and d¹⁰ ions are generally colourless and diamagnetic because they lack partially filled d levels or unpaired electrons.

known_pitfalls.claim: Lanthanoid contraction is caused by strong shielding by 4f electrons.
known_pitfalls.correction: It results from poor shielding of increasing nuclear charge by 4f electrons, causing a gradual decrease in size.

known_pitfalls.claim: KMnO₄ and K₂Cr₂O₇ have the same reduction products in every medium.
known_pitfalls.correction: Their reduction products depend on the medium; for example, permanganate gives Mn²⁺ in acid, MnO₂ in neutral or weakly alkaline medium and manganate in strongly alkaline medium.

recommended_example_progression: Start with NCERT Example 4.1 on why Sc is a transition element but Zn is not.
Use NCERT Example 4.2 to relate unpaired electrons to enthalpy of atomisation.
Apply NCERT Examples 4.3–4.7 to oxidation-state stability and electrode potentials.
Use NCERT Example 4.8 to calculate spin-only magnetic moment.
Finish with NCERT Examples 4.9 and 4.10 on disproportionation and lanthanoid oxidation states.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The end-of-chapter Exercises are numbered 4.1 to 4.38 and cover configurations, oxidation states, electrode potentials, magnetic moments, dichromate, permanganate, lanthanoid contraction and actinoid chemistry.
